subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Is the source-level accepted-before-sandbox-start path plus the linked Docker duplicate enough to queue a fix, or should maintainers require a fresh live Docker reproduction on current main before repair starts?
rationale: The central symptom is credible and supported by source/discussion evidence, but the repair crosses async spawn admission, sandbox startup, terminal session state, and an open lifecycle-design issue, so automation should not choose the proof bar alone.

options.title: Require live Docker proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a forced Docker-backed `sessions_spawn` repro on current main before deciding the exact repair shape.

options.title: Queue a narrow repair from source evidence
options.body: Let a repair PR add forced-failure tests and terminalize/log sandbox startup failures without waiting for a manual live repro.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle tracker
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 as the only remaining work if maintainers decide startup lifecycle signals fully cover this sandbox symptom.

recommendation.title: Require live Docker proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a forced Docker-backed `sessions_spawn` repro on current main before deciding the exact repair shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blamed maintenance and broad agent/gateway ownership history make steipete the best available routing owner for the proof-bar decision.
